title: Outbound contact runtime configuration boundary
purpose: Define the canonical server-owned runtime configuration contract for outbound insurance contact while preserving fail-closed behavior and performing no provider activation or network execution.

currentState.privateRoute: src/pages/river-os/actions/insurance-contact.ts remains fail closed and supplies no provider composition.
currentState.telnyxAdapter: Existing Telnyx adapter requires apiKey, connectionId, and fromNumber.
currentState.runtime: No canonical outbound provider runtime configuration contract currently exists.

configuration.enableGate: INSURANCE_OUTBOUND_CONTACT_ENABLED must equal true before any outbound provider may be considered enabled.
configuration.providerSelector: INSURANCE_CONTACT_PROVIDER identifies the explicitly selected provider; initial supported configured value may be telnyx.
configuration.ownership: All configuration is server-owned and must never be accepted from browser form input.
configuration.failClosed: Missing, malformed, partial, unsupported, or disabled configuration resolves to no outbound provider composition.

requirements: Introduce a pure runtime-configuration parser/resolver boundary before any provider construction.
Do not instantiate Telnyx or any concrete provider in INS-007U.
Do not modify the private contact route to execute requestContact.
Require both the explicit enable gate and provider selector before provider-specific configuration can be considered.
Require complete provider-specific configuration; partial credentials must fail closed.
Never expose secrets, provider references, destinations, credentials, timestamps, attempt state, or idempotency controls to browser input.
Keep provider selection and credentials server-side only.
Add focused tests for disabled, missing, partial, unsupported, and valid configuration parsing without performing network calls.
boundaries: No live call, SMS, or email.
No Telnyx account configuration or purchase.
No routing, scoring, or automatic producer assignment.
nextBoundary: A later explicitly authorized slice may compose a validated runtime configuration into a concrete provider and then separately authorize route execution.
